```{r setup, include=FALSE}

# SETTING UP LIBRARIES
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(Metrics)
library(forecast)
library(glmnet)
```

## Loading Datasets
```{r}

data = read.csv("../data/data_merged.csv")
data_mean = read.csv("../data/prevail_mean.csv")

data$date <- as.Date(data$date)
data_mean$date <- as.Date(data_mean$date)

data <- data %>%
  select(
    date,
    log_ret,
    matches("^price_fd_L[1-5]$"),
    matches("^log_ret_L[1-5]$"),
    matches("_L[2-5]$")       # only lagged features from at least 2 periods ago
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    data_mean %>% select(date, mean_prevailing_ret),
    by = "date"
  )

```

## Ridge Regression Model

# ============================================================================
# MODELING APPROACH: 80/20 Train-Test Split w/ Recursive CV
# ============================================================================

```{r}
# --- STEP 1: Prepare data ---

ridge_df <- data %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  select(-mean_prevailing_ret) %>%
  drop_na()

set.seed(123)

n <- nrow(ridge_df)
train_size <- floor(0.8 * n)  # 80% training
test_size <- n - train_size   # 20% testing

cat("\n=== Data Split ===\n")
cat("Training:", train_size, "observations\n")
cat("Testing :", test_size, "observations\n")

train_data <- ridge_df[1:train_size, ]
test_data  <- ridge_df[(train_size + 1):n, ]

# Extract features and target
X_train <- train_data %>% select(-date, -log_ret) %>% as.matrix()
y_train <- train_data$log_ret

X_test <- test_data %>% select(-date, -log_ret) %>% as.matrix()
y_test <- test_data$log_ret

cat("\nFeatures in model:", ncol(X_train), "\n")

```

## Helper Functions: BIC-based Lambda Selection

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# BIC-based Lambda Selection Functions (Kock & Callot)
# BIC(λ) = log(RSS(λ)) + (log(T)/T)·df(λ)
# ============================================================================

# Function 1: Compute degrees of freedom for Ridge Regression
# df(λ) = Σ_i d_i^2/(d_i^2+λ) where d_i are singular values of standardized X
compute_ridge_df <- function(X_standardized, lambda) {
  # Singular value decomposition
  svd_result <- svd(X_standardized)
  d <- svd_result$d  # singular values
  
  # df(λ) = sum(d_i^2 / (d_i^2 + λ))
  df <- sum((d^2) / (d^2 + lambda))
  
  return(df)
}

# Function 2: Fit Ridge Regression and compute BIC for each lambda
fit_ridge_bic <- function(X, y, alpha = 0, lambdas = NULL) {
  
  # ---- Input validation ----
  T <- nrow(X)
  
  if (length(y) != T) stop("X and y must have same number of rows")
  if (!is.matrix(X)) X <- as.matrix(X)
  
  # ---- Standardize X (glmnet standardizes internally, but we do it for df calculation) ----
  X_mean <- colMeans(X)
  X_sd <- apply(X, 2, sd)
  X_std <- scale(X, center = X_mean, scale = X_sd)
  
  # Fit glmnet (ridge: alpha=0, standardize=TRUE, intercept=TRUE)
  fit <- glmnet(X, y, alpha = alpha, standardize = TRUE, intercept = TRUE, 
                lambda = lambdas, thresh = 1e-7)
  
  # ---- Compute RSS on training data ----
  # Get predictions for each lambda
  y_pred_matrix <- predict(fit, newx = X, s = fit$lambda)
  
  # RSS for each lambda
  RSS_vec <- colSums((y - y_pred_matrix)^2)
  
  # ---- Compute degrees of freedom for each lambda ----
  df_vec <- sapply(fit$lambda, function(lam) {
    compute_ridge_df(X_std, lam)
  })
  
  # ---- Compute BIC: log(RSS) + (log(T)/T) * df ----
  bic_penalty <- log(T) / T
  BIC_vec <- log(RSS_vec) + bic_penalty * df_vec
  
  # ---- Find optimal lambda ----
  idx_best <- which.min(BIC_vec)
  lambda_best <- fit$lambda[idx_best]
  
  # ---- Create results table ----
  bic_tbl <- data.frame(
    lambda = fit$lambda,
    RSS = RSS_vec,
    df = df_vec,
    BIC = BIC_vec,
    is_best = (fit$lambda == lambda_best)
  )
  
  # ---- Return results ----
  return(list(
    lambda_best = lambda_best,
    bic_tbl = bic_tbl,
    fit = fit,
    X_mean = X_mean,
    X_sd = X_sd
  ))
}

# Function 3: Helper to select lambda by BIC
# Dispatches based on alpha (0=Ridge, 1=Lasso)
select_lambda_bic <- function(X, y, alpha = 0, lambdas = NULL) {
  
  if (is.null(lambdas)) {
    # Generate default lambda sequence (glmnet default behavior)
    lambdas <- 10^seq(5, -2, length.out = 100)
  }
  
  if (alpha == 0) {
    # Ridge Regression
    result <- fit_ridge_bic(X, y, alpha = 0, lambdas = lambdas)
  } else if (alpha == 1) {
    # LASSO (not implemented yet, but structure ready)
    stop("LASSO not yet implemented. Use alpha=0 for Ridge.")
  } else {
    stop("alpha must be 0 (Ridge) or 1 (LASSO)")
  }
  
  return(result)
}

```

## Example: Ridge Regression with BIC Lambda Selection

```{r}
# ---- Fit Ridge Regression using BIC for lambda selection ----

# Generate lambda sequence (smaller grid)
lambdas <- 10^seq(5, -2, length.out = 100)

# Fit ridge with BIC
ridge_result <- select_lambda_bic(X_train, y_train, alpha = 0, lambdas = lambdas)

cat("\n=== Ridge Regression: BIC-based Lambda Selection ===\n")
cat("Optimal λ:", round(ridge_result$lambda_best, 6), "\n")
cat("Training size (T):", nrow(X_train), "\n")

# Display top 10 lambdas by BIC
top_bics <- ridge_result$bic_tbl %>%
  arrange(BIC) %>%
  head(10)

cat("\nTop 10 λ values by BIC:\n")
print(top_bics)

```

```{r}
# ---- Predict on test set ----

# Extract the fitted model
fit <- ridge_result$fit
lambda_opt <- ridge_result$lambda_best

# Predict on test data
y_pred_test <- predict(fit, newx = X_test, s = lambda_opt)

# Compute test metrics
mae_ridge <- mae(y_test, y_pred_test)
rmse_ridge <- rmse(y_test, y_pred_test)
r2_ridge <- cor(y_test, y_pred_test)^2

cat("\n=== Ridge Regression Test Performance ===\n")
cat("MAE :", round(mae_ridge, 6), "\n")
cat("RMSE:", round(rmse_ridge, 6), "\n")
cat("R²  :", round(r2_ridge, 4), "\n")

```

```{r}
# ---- Visualize BIC curve ----

ggplot(ridge_result$bic_tbl, aes(x = log10(lambda), y = BIC)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = ridge_result$bic_tbl %>% filter(is_best), 
             color = "red", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Ridge Regression: BIC vs Log10(λ)",
    x = "Log10(λ)",
    y = "BIC",
    subtitle = paste("Optimal λ =", round(ridge_result$lambda_best, 6))
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "italic"))

```

```{r}
# ---- Extract and display coefficients ----

# Get coefficients at optimal lambda
coefs <- coef(fit, s = lambda_opt)

# Convert to data frame for better display
coefs_df <- data.frame(
  feature = rownames(coefs),
  coefficient = as.numeric(coefs)
)

# Extract and display intercept
intercept <- coefs_df %>% filter(feature == "(Intercept)") %>% pull(coefficient)

cat("\n=== Ridge Regression Intercept (λ =", round(lambda_opt, 6), ") ===\n")
cat("Intercept:", round(intercept, 8), "\n")

# Remove intercept row for feature coefficients display
coefs_df <- coefs_df %>% filter(feature != "(Intercept)")

# Sort by absolute value for easier interpretation
coefs_df <- coefs_df %>%
  mutate(abs_coef = abs(coefficient)) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs_coef))

cat("\n=== Ridge Regression Coefficients (λ =", round(lambda_opt, 6), ") ===\n")
print(coefs_df)

```

```{r}
# ---- Visualize coefficients ----

ggplot(coefs_df, aes(x = reorder(feature, coefficient), y = coefficient, fill = coefficient > 0)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("steelblue", "coral"), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Ridge Regression Coefficients",
    x = "Feature",
    y = "Coefficient Value"
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
# ---- Visualize forecasted vs actual returns on test set ----

# Create a data frame for plotting
test_results <- data.frame(
  date = test_data$date,
  actual = y_test,
  forecasted = as.numeric(y_pred_test),
  obs_num = seq_along(y_test)
)

# Line plot: Forecasted vs Actual
ggplot(test_results, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = actual, color = "Actual"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = forecasted, color = "Ridge Forecast"), linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Ridge Regression: Forecasted vs Actual Returns (Test Set)",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Log Return",
    color = "Series"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Actual" = "steelblue", "Ridge Forecast" = "coral")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

```

```{r}
# ---- Scatter plot: Forecasted vs Actual ----

ggplot(test_results, aes(x = actual, y = forecasted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Ridge Regression: Forecast Accuracy (Test Set)",
    x = "Actual Return",
    y = "Forecasted Return",
    subtitle = paste("R² =", round(r2_ridge, 4), "| RMSE =", round(rmse_ridge, 6))
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1)

```

```{r}
# ---- Save Ridge Regression Predictions and Results ----

# Create results dataframe with TRAINING predictions
y_pred_train <- predict(fit, newx = X_train, s = lambda_opt)

ridge_train_predictions <- data.frame(
  date = train_data$date,
  ridge_actual = y_train,
  ridge_forecast = as.numeric(y_pred_train)
)

# Save training predictions to CSV
write.csv(ridge_train_predictions, "../data/ridge_train_predictions.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Create results dataframe with TEST predictions
ridge_predictions <- test_results %>%
  select(date, actual, forecasted) %>%
  rename(
    ridge_forecast = forecasted,
    ridge_actual = actual
  )

# Save test predictions to CSV
write.csv(ridge_predictions, "../data/ridge_predictions.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Save model evaluation metrics
ridge_metrics <- data.frame(
  model = "Ridge Regression",
  optimal_lambda = ridge_result$lambda_best,
  MAE = mae_ridge,
  RMSE = rmse_ridge,
  R2 = r2_ridge
)

cat("\n=== Ridge Regression Results Saved ===\n")

cat("✓ Metrics saved to: ../data/ridge_metrics.csv\n")
cat("✓ BIC table saved to: ../data/ridge_bic_table.csv\n")

```
